sections.title: Stringing sentences into a story
sections.content: aztán ("then") and utána ("after that") chain past-tense clauses together the same way you already use them for anything sequential — just now every clause is in the past instead of the present or imperative. Reggel bevásároltam, aztán találkoztam Petrával a piacon. strings two whole sentences together with one word. utána works the same way but leans slightly more on "after that happened" than aztán's plain "then": Ettünk egy kávézóban. Utána hazamentünk.

sections.title: aztán vs. utána
rows: I went shopping in the morning, then met Petra.
I bought the gift. After that I went home.
I drank coffee, then went off to work.

items.spanish: Előbb találkoztam Tamással, aztán vettem egy ajándékot Ildikónak.
items.english: First I met Tamás, then I bought a gift for Ildikó.

items.spanish: Láttuk a filmet, utána beszélgettünk róla.
items.english: We saw the movie, and after that we talked about it.
I did the shopping, then took the bag home.

sections.content: You don't need to repeat the subject with aztán or utána — one shared (én)/(mi)/(ő) covers the whole chain, which is exactly what makes these two words feel so natural for telling a short story.
